# N25: Who may speak for a review: a non-member reads and is told who can add them; a member and an admin speak

A check of the core ([the journeys](../journeys.md)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/notes/13-review-speak.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured, and a limit its words don’t give is added after it, in the script’s test (“its test: …”).

## What it checks

who may speak for a review (RV7, docs/design/reviews/spec.md section 3). [REVIEW-SPEAK] Someone not in a review reads it but can't speak for it: its page has no primary button and no Join it would refuse, and says who can add them; a goal opened in its walk offers nothing to say. Someone in it, and an admin, get the review's own buttons.

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day. {…} is a value the script works out as it runs.

## What it reports as wrong

- {w}: someone not in the review has a primary button on its page (passes when `p.locator('.review-home .btn.primary').count() === 0`)
- {w}: the review still offers Join
- {w}: the page doesn’t say who can add them (“{hero.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 200)}”)
- {w}: {who} is told they aren’t in the review
